akhfash:9-11.t: He said ﴿يَوْمَ تَمُورُ ٱلسَّمَآءُ مَوْراً﴾ ﴿وَتَسِيرُ ٱلْجِبَالُ سَيْراً﴾ ﴿فَوَيْلٌ﴾: the fāʾ came in because it has the meaning of "when such-and-such happens", so it resembles the conditional, because the conditional has its khabar (apodosis) with fāʾ.

akhfash:30-30.t: And He said ﴿نَّتَرَبَّصُ بِهِ رَيْبَ ٱلْمَنُونِ﴾ because you say: "تَرَبَّصْتُ زَيْداً" (I waited for Zayd), i.e. I waited for him (تربصت به).

daas-irab:1-12.t: ﴿وَالطُّورِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being "أقسم". ﴿وَكِتابٍ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الطور. ﴿مَسْطُورٍ﴾ an adjective. ﴿فِي رَقٍّ﴾ the two are attached to مسطور. ﴿مَنْشُورٍ﴾ an adjective. ﴿وَالْبَيْتِ الْمَعْمُورِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَالسَّقْفِ الْمَرْفُوعِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَالْبَحْرِ الْمَسْجُورِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿إِنَّ عَذابَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿لَواقِعٌ﴾ the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and واقع is the khabar (predicate) of inna; the clause is the answer to the first oath. ﴿ما﴾ negating. ﴿لَهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, an advanced khabar. ﴿مِنْ دافِعٍ﴾ min is a redundant (zāʾid) preposition, and دافع is genitive in form, nominative in position, a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is a second khabar of inna. ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿تَمُورُ السَّماءُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿مَوْراً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿وَتَسِيرُ الْجِبالُ سَيْراً﴾ conjoined to what precedes it, and its i'rab is clear. ﴿فَوَيْلٌ﴾ a particle of resumption, and a mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ an adverb of time annexed to an adverb like it. ﴿لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ; the clause is resumptive. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ an adjective of المكذبين. ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿فِي خَوْضٍ﴾ the two are attached to يلعبون. ﴿يَلْعَبُونَ﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين.

daas-irab:13-18.t: ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ a badal (substitute) from يومئذ. ﴿يُدَعُّونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿إِلى نارِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿جَهَنَّمَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿دَعًّا﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿هذِهِ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿النَّارُ﴾ khabar (predicate). ﴿الَّتِي﴾ an adjective of النار. ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿بِها﴾ the two are attached to what follows them. ﴿تُكَذِّبُونَ﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the khabar of كنتم, and the clause كنتم is the ṣila (relative clause) of التي. ﴿أَفَسِحْرٌ﴾ the hamza is a particle of disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī), the fāʾ is a conjunction, and an advanced khabar. ﴿هذا﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَمْ﴾ in the sense of bal. ﴿أَنْتُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿لا﴾ a particle of negation. ﴿تُبْصِرُونَ﴾ a nominative imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿اصْلَوْها﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil and hā its mafʿūl (object). ﴿فَاصْبِرُوا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَوْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿لا تَصْبِرُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lā of prohibition, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿سَواءٌ﴾ the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "your patience and its absence are alike". ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ the two are attached to سواء. ﴿إِنَّما﴾ the restraining (kāffa) and the restrained (makfūfa). ﴿تُجْزَوْنَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil; the clause is an explanation of cause (taʿlīl). ﴿ما﴾ relative, a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ a nominative imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of كنتم, and the clause كنتم is the ṣila of mā. ﴿إِنَّ الْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿فِي جَنَّاتٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, its khabar. ﴿وَنَعِيمٍ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to جنات; the clause is resumptive. ﴿فاكِهِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb) by the yāʾ. ﴿بِما﴾ the two are attached to فاكهين. ﴿آتاهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl. ﴿رَبُّهُمْ﴾ a postponed fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila of mā. ﴿وَوَقاهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ﴾ conjoined to آتاهم ربهم. ﴿عَذابَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿الْجَحِيمِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi.

daas-irab:19-24.t: ﴿كُلُوا﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the object of an omitted saying. ﴿وَاشْرَبُوا﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to كلوا. ﴿هَنِيئاً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿بِما﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) كلوا. ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of كنتم, and the clause كنتم is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿مُتَّكِئِينَ﴾ ḥāl, accusative (manṣūb) by the yāʾ. ﴿عَلى سُرُرٍ﴾ the two are attached to the ḥāl. ﴿مَصْفُوفَةٍ﴾ an adjective of سرر. ﴿وَزَوَّجْناهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl (object). ﴿بِحُورٍ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿عِينٍ﴾ an adjective of حور; the clause is conjoined to His words في جنات. ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila of الذين. ﴿وَاتَّبَعَتْهُمْ ذُرِّيَّتُهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its mafʿūl and a postponed fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿بِإِيمانٍ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿أَلْحَقْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿بِهِمْ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿ذُرِّيَّتُهُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the khabar of الذين. [Translator's note: the source vowels this word with ḍamma (ذُرِّيَّتُهُمْ); as mafʿūl bihi it is ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ.] ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and mā is negating. ﴿أَلَتْناهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿مِنْ عَمَلِهِمْ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿مِنْ شَيْءٍ﴾ min is redundant (zāʾida); شيء is genitive in form, accusative in position, a second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿كُلُّ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿امْرِئٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿بِما﴾ the two are attached to رهين. ﴿كَسَبَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿رَهِينٌ﴾ the khabar of كل; the verbal clause is the ṣila of mā, and the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿وَأَمْدَدْناهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿بِفاكِهَةٍ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿وَلَحْمٍ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿مِمَّا﴾ the two are attached to an omitted adjective of لحم. ﴿يَشْتَهُونَ﴾ a nominative imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿يَتَنازَعُونَ﴾ a nominative imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿فِيها﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿كَأْساً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿لا﴾ negating, without governing effect (muhmala). ﴿لَغْوٌ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿فِيها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, its khabar; the clause is an adjective of كأس. ﴿وَلا تَأْثِيمٌ﴾ conjoined to لا لغو. ﴿وَيَطُوفُ﴾ a nominative imperfect verb. ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿غِلْمانٌ﴾ fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted adjective of غلمان. ﴿كَأَنَّهُمْ لُؤْلُؤٌ﴾ kaʾanna, its noun and its khabar. ﴿مَكْنُونٌ﴾ an adjective of لؤلؤ; the clause is an adjective of غلمان.

daas-irab:25-31.t: ﴿وَأَقْبَلَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; a past verb. ﴿بَعْضُهُمْ﴾ fāʿil (agent). ﴿عَلى بَعْضٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿يَتَساءَلُونَ﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿كُنَّا﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿قَبْلُ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿فِي أَهْلِنا﴾ the two are attached to what follows them. ﴿مُشْفِقِينَ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of kāna; the clause كنا is the khabar of inna, and the clause إنا is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿فَمَنَّ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿عَلَيْنا﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿وَوَقانا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb and its mafʿūl (object); the fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿عَذابَ﴾ a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿السَّمُومِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿كُنَّا﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ the two are attached to ندعوه; the clause كنا is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause إنا is the object of saying. ﴿نَدْعُوهُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl; the clause is the khabar of كنا. ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿هُوَ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). ﴿الْبَرُّ الرَّحِيمُ﴾ two predicates; the nominal clause is explanatory of cause (taʿlīliyya) and has no grammatical position. ﴿فَذَكِّرْ﴾ the fāʾ is a particle of resumption, and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَما﴾ the fāʾ is a particle of causation, and mā is negating, operating like laysa. ﴿أَنْتَ﴾ its noun. ﴿بِنِعْمَةِ﴾ the two are attached to the negation conveyed by mā. ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿بِكاهِنٍ﴾ genitive in form, accusative in position as the khabar of mā. ﴿وَلا مَجْنُونٍ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it; the clause ما أنت is an explanation of cause (taʿlīl). ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction in the sense of bal. ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ a nominative imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿شاعِرٌ﴾ the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "هو شاعر"; the nominal clause is the object of saying. ﴿نَتَرَبَّصُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is an adjective. ﴿بِهِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿رَيْبَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿الْمَنُونِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿تَرَبَّصُوا﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the object of saying. ﴿فَإِنِّي﴾ the fāʾ is for causation, and inna and its noun. ﴿مَعَكُمْ﴾ an adverb of place. ﴿مِنَ الْمُتَرَبِّصِينَ﴾ the khabar of inna; the nominal clause is an explanation of cause.

daas-irab:32-38.t: ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿تَأْمُرُهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl (object). ﴿أَحْلامُهُمْ﴾ fāʿil (agent); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿بِهذا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿هُمْ قَوْمٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). ﴿طاغُونَ﴾ an adjective; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿تَقَوَّلَهُ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿بَلْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿لا﴾ negating. ﴿يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ a nominative imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَلْيَأْتُوا﴾ the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (fāʾ of elucidation), and an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lām of command, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the implied (muqaddar) condition. ﴿بِحَدِيثٍ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿مِثْلِهِ﴾ an adjective. ﴿إِنْ﴾ conditional, governing the jussive. ﴿كانُوا صادِقِينَ﴾ kāna, its noun and its khabar; the clause is initial. ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿خُلِقُوا﴾ a passive past verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿مِنْ غَيْرِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿هُمُ الْخالِقُونَ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿خَلَقُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿السَّماواتِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَالْأَرْضَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of conjunction and digression (iḍrāb). ﴿لا﴾ negating. ﴿يُوقِنُونَ﴾ a nominative imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿عِنْدَهُمْ﴾ an adverb of place attached to an omitted, advanced khabar. ﴿خَزائِنُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿هُمُ الْمُصَيْطِرُونَ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ an advanced khabar. ﴿سُلَّمٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿يَسْتَمِعُونَ﴾ a nominative imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿فِيهِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb; the clause is an adjective of سلم. ﴿فَلْيَأْتِ﴾ the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, and an imperfect verb, jussive by the lām of command, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter. ﴿مُسْتَمِعُهُمْ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿بِسُلْطانٍ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿مُبِينٍ﴾ an adjective of سلطان; the verbal clause is the apodosis of a condition that does not govern the jussive.

daas-irab:39-42.t: ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿لَهُ﴾ an advanced khabar (predicate). ﴿الْبَناتُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَلَكُمُ﴾ an advanced khabar. ﴿الْبَنُونَ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative (marfūʿ) by the wāw because it is treated like the sound masculine plural; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿تَسْئَلُهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl (object), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿أَجْراً﴾ a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿فَهُمْ﴾ a conjunction and a mubtadaʾ. ﴿مِنْ مَغْرَمٍ﴾ the two (preposition and genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) what follows them. ﴿مُثْقَلُونَ﴾ khabar; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿عِنْدَهُمُ﴾ an adverb of place attached to an omitted, advanced khabar. ﴿الْغَيْبُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿فَهُمْ﴾ a conjunction and a mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَكْتُبُونَ﴾ a nominative imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿يُرِيدُونَ﴾ a nominative imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿كَيْداً﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَالَّذِينَ﴾ a particle of resumption and a mubtadaʾ. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين. ﴿هُمُ الْمَكِيدُونَ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and khabar; the nominal clause is the khabar of الذين.

daas-irab:43-45.t: ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ an advanced khabar (predicate). ﴿إِلهٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿غَيْرُ﴾ an adjective. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿سُبْحانَ﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿عَمَّا﴾ the two (preposition and genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) سبحان. ﴿يُشْرِكُونَ﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of mā. ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ the wāw is a particle of resumption, and in is a conditional particle governing the jussive. ﴿يَرَوْا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿كِسْفاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿مِنَ السَّماءِ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted adjective of كسفا. ﴿ساقِطاً﴾ a second adjective of كسفا; the clause is initial and has no grammatical position. ﴿يَقُولُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause has no grammatical position because it is not joined with the fāʾ. ﴿سَحابٌ﴾ the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. ﴿مَرْكُومٌ﴾ an adjective; the nominal clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿فَذَرْهُمْ﴾ the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (fāʾ of elucidation), and an imperative verb and its mafʿūl, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is the apodosis of an implied (muqaddar) condition and has no grammatical position. ﴿حَتَّى﴾ a particle of limit and genitive. ﴿يُلاقُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an concealed after ḥattā, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿يَوْمَهُمُ﴾ its mafʿūl; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from an and what follows it is in the position of the genitive by ḥattā, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb ذرهم. ﴿الَّذِي﴾ an adjective of يومهم. ﴿فِيهِ﴾ the two are attached to what follows them. ﴿يُصْعَقُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the ṣila of الذي.

daas-irab:46-49.t: ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ a badal (substitute) from يومهم. ﴿لا﴾ negating. ﴿يُغْنِي﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb. ﴿عَنْهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿كَيْدُهُمْ﴾ fāʿil (agent). ﴿شَيْئاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿وَلا﴾ a conjunction, and lā is negating. ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿يُنْصَرُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of هم, and the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَإِنَّ﴾ the wāw is a particle of resumption, and inna is a particle resembling the verb. ﴿لِلَّذِينَ﴾ an advanced khabar. ﴿ظَلَمُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿عَذاباً﴾ the postponed noun of inna. ﴿دُونَ﴾ an adverb of place. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ﴾ lākinna and its noun. ﴿لا﴾ negating. ﴿يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ a nominative imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the verbal clause is the khabar of lākinna, and the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَاصْبِرْ﴾ the wāw is a particle of resumption, and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive. ﴿لِحُكْمِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَإِنَّكَ﴾ the fāʾ is a particle of causation, and inna and its noun. ﴿بِأَعْيُنِنا﴾ the two are attached to the omitted khabar of inna; the nominal clause is an explanation of cause (taʿlīl). ﴿وَسَبِّحْ﴾ a conjunction, and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿بِحَمْدِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿حِينَ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿تَقُومُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation. ﴿وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ﴾ a conjunction, and a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to what follows them. ﴿فَسَبِّحْهُ﴾ the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and an imperative verb and its mafʿūl (object); the fāʿil is latent. ﴿وَإِدْبارَ﴾ a conjunction, and إدبار is accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ). ﴿النُّجُومِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi.

farraa:1-1.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَٱلطُّورِ﴾.
He swore by it; it is the mountain in Midian beside which Allah, Majestic and Mighty, spoke to Moses, peace be upon him, directly.

farraa:3-3.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿فِي رَقٍّ مَّنْشُورٍ﴾.
«الرَّق» means the scrolls that will be brought out to the children of Adam: one taking his book in his right hand, and another taking his book in his left hand.

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿وَٱلْبَيْتِ ٱلْمَعْمُورِ﴾.
A house that Adam, may Allah bless him, built; it was raised up in the days of the Flood, and it is in the sixth heaven, directly opposite the Kaaba.

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَٱلْبَحْرِ ٱلْمَسْجُورِ﴾.
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah have mercy on him, used to say: kindled with fire. And «المسجور» in the speech of the Arabs means: filled.

farraa:9-9.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿يَوْمَ تَمُورُ ٱلسَّمَآءُ مَوْراً﴾.
It will revolve with what is in it, and the mountains will move off the face of the earth, so that they and the earth become level.

farraa:13-13.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿يَوْمَ يُدَعُّونَ إِلَىٰ نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ ﴾.
They will be shoved. Likewise His saying: ﴿فَذَلِكَ الَّذِى يَدُعُّ الْيَتِيمَ﴾.

farraa:18-18.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿فَاكِهِينَ بِمَآ آتَاهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ﴾.
Delighted with what their Lord has given them.

farraa:21-21.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَٱتَّبَعَتْهُمْ ذُرِّيَّتُهُم﴾: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd read it: (وَاتَّبَعَتْهُمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ). ﴿أَلْحَقْنَا بِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ﴾ in the singular.
He said: Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm told us: al-Farrāʾ told us: Qays and al-Mufaḍḍal al-Ḍabbī told me, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm — al-Mufaḍḍal said: from ʿAlqama, from ʿAbd Allāh; and Qays said: from a man, from ʿAbd Allāh — he said: A man recited to ʿAbd Allāh: "وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَاتّبَعهم ذُرِّيَاتُهم بإِيمانٍ أَلْحَقْنَا بِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّاتِهم". He said: ʿAbd Allāh began reciting it in the singular. He said: until he had repeated it to him about twenty times, without saying "It is not as he says". Al-Ḥasan read both of them in the plural, and some of the people of the Hijaz read the first in the singular and the second in the plural. As for the meaning of His saying ﴿وَٱتَّبَعَتْهُمْ ذُرِّيَّتُهُم﴾, it is said: when the people of Paradise enter Paradise, if the father is of a higher rank than his son, his son is raised to him; and if the child is of higher rank, his father is raised to him. [57/ا] And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَمَآ أَلَتْنَاهُمْ﴾.
«الألْت» means diminishing. There is another dialectal form of it: (وما لِتْناهم من عَملِهم من شىء), and it is so in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh and of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb. The poet said:
أبلغْ بنى ثُمَلٍ عنِّى مُغَلْغَلَة * جَهْدَ الرسالةِ لا أَلْتاً ولا كذِبا
(Convey from me to the Banū Thumal a far-travelling message, the message in full, with no diminishing and no lie.)
He means: no diminishing and no adding. Another said:
وليلةٍ ذات نَدىً سَرَيتُ * ولم يَلتْنى عن سُرَاها لَيْتُ
(Many a dewy night I have travelled, and no holding back (layt) kept me from travelling it.)
«اللَّيْت» here is a maṣdar (verbal noun): no deficiency in me and no inability for it turned me away from it.

farraa:28-28.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿إِنَّا كُنَّا مِن قَبْلُ نَدْعُوهُ﴾.
«إِنَّه»: ʿĀṣim, al-Aʿmash and al-Ḥasan read it (إِنَّه) with a kasra on the alif, and Abū Jaʿfar al-Madanī and Nāfiʿ read it (أنَّه). Whoever gives it a kasra begins a new sentence (istaʾnafa); whoever gives it a fatḥa means: «we used to call upon Him because He is the Beneficent, the Merciful», and that is a good reading. Al-Farrāʾ said: al-Kisāʾī reads (أنَّه) with a fatḥa, while I read it with a kasra; I only said "good" because al-Kisāʾī read it so.

farraa:30-30.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿نَّتَرَبَّصُ بِهِ رَيْبَ ٱلْمَنُونِ ﴾.
The afflictions of time, so that he will be kept busy away from you and his companions will scatter; or the lifespan of his forefathers, for we know their lifespans.

farraa:32-32.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿أَمْ تَأْمُرُهُمْ أَحْلاَمُهُمْ بِهَـٰذَآ﴾.
«الأحلام» in this place means minds and intellects.

farraa:37-37.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿ٱلْمُصَيْطِرُونَ﴾, and ﴿لَسْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِمُصَيْطِرٍ﴾.
[57/ب] It is written with ṣād, and it is read both with sīn and with ṣād. Al-Kisāʾī read it with sīn. Similar to it are «بصطة» and «بسطة»: some of them are written with ṣād and some with sīn, and the reading is with sīn in «بَسْطة» and «يَبْسُط» — and all of that, I believe he said, is correct.
Al-Farrāʾ said: in the codices (maṣāḥif), in al-Baqara it is written «بَسْطةً», and in al-Aʿrāf «بصطةً» with ṣād, and in the rest of the Quran it is written with sīn.

farraa:45-45.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿حَتَّىٰ يُلاَقُواْ يَوْمَهُمُ﴾ with the alif. Some read (يَلْقَوْا), but «الملاقاة» is the more eloquent Arabic, and both are good.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فِيهِ يُصْعَقُونَ﴾: ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash read it (يَصعقون) [and the people of the Hijaz (يُصعقون)], and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read it (يَصعقون) with a fatḥa on the yāʾ, like al-Aʿmash.
«[Translator's note: the source attributes «يَصعقون» (with fatḥa) to ʿĀṣim; in the received transmission ʿĀṣim reads «يُصعقون» with a ḍamma.]»
The Arabs say «صُعِق الرجُلُ» and «صَعِق», and «سُعِد» and «سَعِدَ»; these are dialectal forms, all of them correct.

zajjaj:25-25.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأقْبَلَ بَعْضُهم عَلى بَعْضٍ يَتَساءَلُونَ﴾ ﴿قالُوا إنّا كُنّا قَبْلُ في أهْلِنا مُشْفِقِينَ﴾ [al-Ṭūr: 26]: the wording — and Allah knows best — indicates here that they ask one another in Paradise about the states they were in during the life of this world; one of them would say to another: "By what did you come to this lofty rank?" And there is evidence for this in the wording, namely His saying — in answer to the question —: ﴿إنّا كُنّا قَبْلُ في أهْلِنا مُشْفِقِينَ﴾ [al-Ṭūr: 26], that is: fearful of ending up in the punishment of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, so we acted in obedience to Him. Then, together with that, they joined to the answer sincerity and the affirmation of His oneness (tawḥīd), by their saying: ﴿إنّا كُنّا مِن قَبْلُ نَدْعُوهُ إنَّهُ هو البَرُّ الرَّحِيمُ﴾ [al-Ṭūr: 28], that is: we used to affirm His oneness, and we did not call upon any god other than Him.

zajjaj:27-27.t: ﴿فَمَنَّ اللَّهُ عَلَيْنا ووَقانا عَذابَ السَّمُومِ﴾, that is: the punishment of the scorching wind (samūm) of Hell.

zajjaj:29-29.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَذَكِّرْ فَما أنْتَ بِنِعْمَتِ رَبِّكَ بِكاهِنٍ ولا مَجْنُونٍ﴾, that is: remind them of what We have prepared for the God-fearing believers and for the misguided disbelievers. ﴿فَما أنْتَ بِنِعْمَتِ رَبِّكَ بِكاهِنٍ ولا مَجْنُونٍ﴾, that is: you do not say what you say as soothsaying, and you do not speak except by revelation from Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.

zajjaj:30-30.t: And His saying: ﴿أمْ يَقُولُونَ شاعِرٌ نَتَرَبَّصُ بِهِ رَيْبَ المَنُونِ﴾: "رَيْبَ المَنُونِ" means the vicissitudes of time.

zajjaj:31-31.t: ﴿قُلْ تَرَبَّصُوا فَإنِّي مَعَكم مِنَ المُتَرَبِّصِينَ﴾: it has come in the exegesis that those who said this — and Abū Jahl was among them — all perished before the death of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

zajjaj:32-32.t: And His saying: ﴿أمْ تَأْمُرُهم أحْلامُهم بِهَذا أمْ هم قَوْمٌ طاغُونَ﴾, that is: do their minds command them to refuse acceptance from one who calls them to the affirmation of Allah's oneness and brings them proofs for that, while they fashion stones and worship them? ﴿أمْ هم قَوْمٌ طاغُونَ﴾, that is: or do they disbelieve out of transgression, when the truth has become clear to them?

zajjaj:34-34.t: ﴿فَلْيَأْتُوا بِحَدِيثٍ مِثْلِهِ﴾, that is: if they say that the Prophet ﷺ fabricated it, then they have claimed that it is human speech, so let them say the like of it. Yet not one of them attempted to say the like of ten surahs, nor the like of a single surah.

zajjaj:35-35.t: And His saying: ﴿أمْ خُلِقُوا مِن غَيْرِ شَيْءٍ أمْ هُمُ الخالِقُونَ﴾: its meaning is: "Rather, were they created from nothing?" There are two views on this verse, and it is among the most difficult things in this surah. One of the philologists said: "They are not stronger in creation than the creation of the heavens and the earth, because the heavens and the earth were created from nothing, whereas they were created from Adam, and Adam from dust." And another view has been stated about it: ﴿أمْ خُلِقُوا مِن غَيْرِ شَيْءٍ﴾ means "or were they created for nothing?", that is: were they created in vain, not to be called to account, nor commanded, nor forbidden?

zajjaj:37-37.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أمْ عِنْدَهم خَزائِنُ رَبِّكَ أمْ هُمُ المُصَيْطِرُونَ﴾: "اَلْمُصَيْطِرُونَ" are the lords who hold dominion. One says: "qad sayṭara ʿalaynā" (he has taken control over us), and "tasayṭara" and "taṣayṭara", with sīn and with ṣād; the original is the sīn, and every sīn followed by a ṭāʾ may be changed into a ṣād. You say "sayṭara" and "ṣayṭara", and "saṭā" and "ṣaṭā". The explanation of ﴿أمْ عِنْدَهم خَزائِنُ رَبِّكَ﴾ is: "Do they have the knowledge that is in the treasuries of your Lord?" And it has been said concerning "خَزائِنُ رَبِّكَ": that is, the provision of your Lord.

zajjaj:38-38.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أمْ لَهم سُلَّمٌ يَسْتَمِعُونَ فِيهِ﴾: the philologists said that the meaning of "يَسْتَمِعُونَ فِيهِ" is "they listen upon it", and similar to it is ﴿وَلأُصَلِّبَنَّكم في جُذُوعِ النَّخْلِ﴾ [Ṭā Hā: 71], that is: upon the trunks of the palm trees. ﴿فَلْيَأْتِ مُسْتَمِعُهم بِسُلْطانٍ مُبِينٍ﴾, that is: with a clear proof. And the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: are they like Jibrīl, who brings the Prophet ﷺ the revelation and makes clear, as His explanation from Allah, what has been and what will be? Then He declared their minds foolish for their assigning daughters to Allah, and said: ﴿أمْ لَهُ البَناتُ ولَكُمُ البَنُونَ﴾ [al-Ṭūr: 39], that is: you assign to Allah what you dislike, while you consider yourselves wise.

zajjaj:40-40.t: ﴿أمْ تَسْألُهم أجْرًا فَهم مِن مَغْرَمٍ مُثْقَلُونَ﴾: the meaning is that the proof is binding upon them from every direction, because you have brought them clear explanation and demonstration, and you have not asked them for any wage for that.

zajjaj:42-42.t: And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿أمْ يُرِيدُونَ كَيْدًا فالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا هُمُ المَكِيدُونَ﴾, that is: "Or do they, in their disbelief and transgression, intend a plot?! For Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, plots against them and requites them for their plotting with punishment in this world and the Hereafter."

zajjaj:43-43.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أمْ لَهم إلَهٌ غَيْرُ اللَّهِ﴾: the meaning is: "Rather, do they have a god other than Allah?!"
If someone asks: They claim that the idols are their gods, so if it is said to them ﴿أمْ لَهم إلَهٌ غَيْرُ اللَّهِ﴾ — [what does it mean]? «[Translator's note: the bracketed words are added for clarity.]» The answer to that is: "Do they have a god other than Allah who creates, provides, and does what created beings are incapable of? For who does that except Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He?" Then He declared Himself transcendent, Mighty and Majestic is He, and said: ﴿سُبْحانَ اللَّهِ عَمّا يُشْرِكُونَ﴾. It has come in the exegesis and in the language that its meaning is: "the declaration of Allah's transcendence above what they associate", that is: above those whom they make partners to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.

zajjaj:44-44.t: And His saying: ﴿وَإنْ يَرَوْا كِسْفًا مِنَ السَّماءِ ساقِطًا يَقُولُوا سَحابٌ مَرْكُومٌ﴾, that is: if they see a piece of the punishment, they say, out of the severity of their transgression and disbelief: "This is heaped-up cloud." "مَرْكُومٌ" means: piled one part upon another. This concerns a group among the leaders of disbelief, and they are those about whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَلَوْ فَتَحْنا عَلَيْهِمْ بابًا مِنَ السَّماءِ فَظَلُّوا فِيهِ يَعْرُجُونَ﴾ [al-Ḥijr: 14] ﴿لَقالُوا إنَّما سُكِّرَتْ أبْصارُنا بَلْ نَحْنُ قَوْمٌ مَسْحُورُونَ﴾ [al-Ḥijr: 15]. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that these people do not take heed, nor attain certainty, nor believe, even with the most dazzling of signs.

zajjaj:45-45.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَذَرْهم حَتّى يُلاقُوا يَوْمَهُمُ الَّذِي فِيهِ يُصْعَقُونَ﴾, and it has also been read ﴿يُصْعَقُونَ﴾ «[Translator's note: the source prints the variant with the same vowelling as the main reading; the variant intended is presumably يَصْعَقُونَ, with fatḥa on the yāʾ.]», that is: leave them until the Day of Resurrection. Then He made known that He will hasten the punishment for them in this world, and said: ﴿وَإنَّ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا عَذابًا دُونَ ذَلِكَ ولَكِنَّ أكْثَرَهم لا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ [al-Ṭūr: 47]. The meaning is: "And indeed for those who do wrong there is a punishment short of the punishment of the Hereafter", meaning the killing, captivity and enslavement of offspring that befell them. And Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that He is the helper of His religion and the destroyer of whoever shows enmity to His Prophet. Then He commanded him to be patient until the punishment befalls them, and said: ﴿واصْبِرْ لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ فَإنَّكَ بِأعْيُنِنا﴾ [al-Ṭūr: 48], that is: for you are where We see you, guard you and watch over you, and they will not reach you with harm. ﴿وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ حِينَ تَقُومُ﴾ [al-Ṭūr: 48], that is: when you rise from your sleep; and it has been said: when you stand in your prayer, and it is what is said together with the opening takbīr: "سُبْحانَكَ اللَّهُمَّ وبِحَمْدِكَ" (Glory be to You, O Allah, and with Your praise).

zajjaj:49-49.t: ﴿وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْهُ وإدْبارَ النُّجُومِ﴾, and it has also been read "وَأدْبارَ النُّجُومِ". Whoever reads "إدْبارَ" with kasra takes it as a maṣdar (verbal noun): "adbartu, idbāran" (I turned away, a turning away); and whoever reads "أدْبارَ" with fatḥa takes it as the plural of "دُبُرٌ" (the back, the end). They agreed in the exegesis that the meaning of "أدْبارَ السُّجُودِ" is the prayer of two rakʿas after the sunset prayer, and that "إدْبارَ النُّجُومِ" is the prayer of the two rakʿas of the dawn.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Ṭūr
Meccan
﷽
His saying: ﴿والطُّورِ﴾ is an oath. "اَلطُّورُ" is the mountain; it has come in the tafsīr (exegesis) that it is the mountain on which Allah spoke to Moses, upon him be peace.

zajjaj:12-12.t: His saying: ﴿الَّذِينَ هم في خَوْضٍ يَلْعَبُونَ﴾, that is: a play whose outcome is punishment keeps them busy through their disbelief.

zajjaj:13-13.t: ﴿يَوْمَ يُدَعُّونَ إلى نارِ جَهَنَّمَ دَعًّا﴾, that is: the day they are driven to it with violent driving and pushed with harsh pushing. From this is His saying: ﴿الَّذِي يَدُعُّ اليَتِيمَ﴾ [al-Māʿūn: 2], that is: he pushes him away from what is due to him.

zajjaj:14-14.t:
His saying: ﴿هَذِهِ النّارُ الَّتِي كُنْتُمْ بِها تُكَذِّبُونَ﴾: the meaning is: "it will be said to them: this is the Fire which you used to deny". ﴿والبَحْرِ المَسْجُورِ﴾ [al-Ṭūr: 6]: it has come in the tafsīr (exegesis) that the sea will be kindled and become the fire of Hell. As for the people of the language, they said: "اَلْبَحْرُ المَسْجُورُ" is the filled sea, and they recited:
؎إذا شاءَ طالَعَ مَسْجُورَةً ∗∗∗ تَرى حَوْلَها النَّبْعَ والسّاسَما
(When he wishes he comes upon a brimming [spring]; you see around it the nabʿ and sāsam trees.)
He means: "you see around it a spring filled with water".

zajjaj:15-15.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أفَسِحْرٌ هَذا أمْ أنْتُمْ لا تُبْصِرُونَ﴾: the form of this alif is the form of the interrogative, and its meaning here is rebuke and reproach, that is: "do you now believe that the punishment of Allah will surely come to pass?"

zajjaj:16-16.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿اصْلَوْها فاصْبِرُوا أوْ لا تَصْبِرُوا سَواءٌ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾: "سَواءٌ" is nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is omitted; the meaning is: "patience and impatience are the same for you".
﴿إنَّما تُجْزَوْنَ ما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾: the meaning of "إنَّما" here is: "you are recompensed only for what you used to do", that is: "the matter proceeds against you with justice; you have been recompensed only for your deeds".

zajjaj:17-17.t:
His saying: ﴿إنَّ المُتَّقِينَ في جَنّاتٍ ونَعِيمٍ﴾ ﴿فاكِهِينَ بِما آتاهم رَبُّهُمْ﴾ [al-Ṭūr: 18] — and "فَكِهِينَ", both [readings] — the accusative is as a ḥāl (circumstantial). The meaning of ﴿فاكِهِينَ بِما آتاهم رَبُّهُمْ﴾ [al-Ṭūr: 18] is: "delighted with what their Lord has given them".
﴿وَوَقاهم رَبُّهم عَذابَ الجَحِيمِ﴾ [al-Ṭūr: 18], that is: He forgave them their sins which would necessitate the Fire, because of their Islam and their repentance.

zajjaj:19-19.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كُلُوا واشْرَبُوا هَنِيئًا بِما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾: the meaning is: "it will be said to them: eat and drink with enjoyment". "هَنِيئًا" is accusative; it is an adjective in the position of the maṣdar (verbal noun). The meaning is: "eat and drink, may you enjoy it with wholesome enjoyment, and may what you have come to be wholesome for you".

zajjaj:2-2.t: ﴿وَكِتابٍ مَسْطُورٍ﴾ ﴿فِي رَقٍّ مَنشُورٍ﴾ [al-Ṭūr: 3]: "اَلْكِتابُ" here is what is recorded against the children of Adam of their deeds.

zajjaj:21-21.t:
His saying: ﴿والَّذِينَ آمَنُوا واتَّبَعَتْهم ذُرِّيَّتُهم بِإيمانٍ ألْحَقْنا بِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ﴾: it has been read "ألْحَقْنا بِهِمْ ذُرِّيّاتِهِمْ", and it has been read "واتَّبَعَتْهم ذُرِّيّاتُهُمْ"; both ways are permissible. "اَلذُّرِّيَّةُ" applies to a group, and "اَلذُّرِّيّاتُ" is a plural; "ذُرِّيَّةٌ" in the singular is more common. The interpretation of the verse is that if the children are believers and the ranks of their fathers in the Garden are higher than their ranks, the children are joined to the fathers, and the fathers are not diminished anything of their deeds; likewise, if the deeds of the fathers are less, the fathers are joined to the children.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَما ألَتْناهم مِن عَمَلِهِمْ مِن شَيْءٍ﴾: its meaning is: We did not diminish them. One says "ألَتَهُ، يَأْلِتُهُ، ألْتًا" when one diminishes him. The poet said:
؎أبْلِغْ بَنِي ثُعَلٍ عَنِّي مُغَلْغَلَةً ∗∗∗ جَهْدَ الرِّسالَةِ لا ألْتًا ولا كَذِبا
(Convey to Banū Thuʿal from me a far-carried message, the full effort of the message, with neither diminution nor lie.)
And one says "لاتَهُ، يَلِيتُهُ، لَيْتًا" when one diminishes him and turns him away from something. The poet said:
؎وَلَيْلَةٍ ذاتِ نَدًى سَرَيْتُ ∗∗∗ ولَمْ يَلِتْنِي عَنْ هَواها لَيْتُ
(Many a dewy night I have travelled through, and no turning-away turned me from my love of it.)

zajjaj:23-23.t:
His saying: ﴿يَتَنازَعُونَ فِيها كَأْسًا لا لَغْوٌ فِيها ولا تَأْثِيمٌ﴾: the meaning of "يَتَنازَعُونَ" is: they pass a cup to one another in it; this one takes the cup from the hand of that one, and that one from the hand of this one.
His saying: ﴿لا لَغْوٌ فِيها ولا تَأْثِيمٌ﴾: its meaning is: nothing that is idle passes between them, that is: neither falsehood nor anything sinful passes between them, as happens in this world among wine-drinkers. "اَلْكَأْسُ" in the language is the filled vessel; if it is empty it is not a kaʾs. It is also read "لا لَغْوَ فِيها ولا تَأْثِيمَ", in the accusative. Whoever puts it in the nominative, it is in two ways: nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), with "فِيها" as the khabar (predicate); or with "لا" in the manner of "لَيْسَ", governing the nominative. Sībawayh and others recited:
؎مَن صَدَّ عَنْ نِيرانِها ∗∗∗ فَأنا ابْنُ قَيْسٍ لا بَراحُ
(Whoever turns away from its fires, I am the son of Qays: there is no leaving.)
Whoever puts it in the accusative, it is by negation and exoneration (tabriʾa, i.e. the lā of generic negation), as in His saying: "لا رَيْبَ فِيهِ"; except that the choice among the grammarians, when "لا" is repeated in this position, is the nominative, while the accusative is, according to all of them, permissible and good.

zajjaj:4-4.t: ﴿والبَيْتِ المَعْمُورِ﴾: In the tafsīr (exegesis) it is a house in heaven opposite the Kaʿba, which seventy thousand angels enter every day, then leave it and never return to it.

zajjaj:7-7.t: His saying: ﴿إنَّ عَذابَ رَبِّكَ لَواقِعٌ﴾ is the jawāb al-qasam (answer of the oath), that is: "by these things, the punishment of your Lord will surely come to pass". It is also possible that the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: "by the Lord of these things, the punishment of your Lord will surely come to pass".

zajjaj:9-9.t:
His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ تَمُورُ السَّماءُ مَوْرًا﴾: "تَمُورُ" means: it revolves. "يَوْمَ" is accusative by His saying: ﴿إنَّ عَذابَ رَبِّكَ لَواقِعٌ﴾ [al-Ṭūr: 7], that is: it will surely come to pass on the Day of Resurrection.
﴿فَوَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ﴾ [al-Ṭūr: 11]: "اَلْوَيْلُ" is a word the Arabs say of everyone who falls into ruin.
